raw_response.blind_rationale:
1. SWiM Family Classification (`none_nonfit`): Excluding S489 from SWiM Families A, B, and C as a reasoned non-fit is strongly justified. In both multivariate logistic regression models (Table 2, PDF p. 8), the dependent variables measure institutional adoption/uptake behavior—household stated `Intent to contract` (Model 1, N = 1,215) and waterpoint user-group `Contract commitment` (signing an annual maintenance contract and paying USD 10/month mobile fees to FundiFix Ltd in 2016; Model 2, N = 254)—rather than realized household or community water service access, functionality, continuity, quality, or affordability. Crucially, 112 waterpoints non-functional for over one year were excluded by design because only already-functioning waterpoints were eligible to contract the service provider (PDF pp. 4–5). Moreover, service-delivery attributes (concern that water is unreliable, electrical conductivity < 1500 uS, pH > 7, distance to next handpump, and concern that water supply is costly) are placed on the right-hand side as predictors of contracting behavior rather than estimated as outcomes of an institutional rule. Consequently, no estimate from Table 2 can be directionally harmonized with household water-access outcomes in Families A, B, or C.

2. Narrow Criterion 2 Assessment (`borderline_governance_or_proxy`): The paper frames its primary institutional comparison around Douglasian cultural-theory "management cultures" (`Individualist` private ownership and `Bureaucratic` school/clinic/religious management vs `Community` management) alongside informal local waterpoint fee and sanctioning rules (`Regular payments`, `Club` fulfilling >=6 of 10 physical/financial/social rules, `Rules made by majority decision`, `Exclusion for not observing rules`, `Penalties for non-payment`, and `In favor of free water for vulnerable`). While pre-existing tariff collection (`Regular payments`), non-payment penalties, exclusion rules, and private/public/community ownership represent concrete local operational/tariff rules, they are informal waterpoint-level routines/governance proxies in an explicitly exploratory, non-causal specification, whereas formal statutory/administrative reforms (Kenya's devolution and Water Act 2016) are discussed only qualitatively in Section 5.3.

3. Criterion 4 Assessment (`borderline_institutional_or_compliance_outcome` / flag for E04/E07 review): Because the tested econometric outcomes (`Intent to contract` and `Contract commitment` to a professional maintenance provider) capture upstream institutional contracting/payment commitment among already-functioning waterpoints rather than realized household water access, coverage, or reliability (and pre-MSP vs free-trial repair downtime of 27 days vs <3 days is reported only descriptively from prior work), the study sits at best on the institutional/behavioral uptake borderline for Criterion 4 and warrants PI verification against E04/E07 if non-access institutional adoption outcomes are excluded.

raw_response.headline_estimate_summary:
Multivariate logistic regressions in Table 2 (PDF p. 8) adjusting for 33–35 organizational, socio-economic, operational, water-use, alternative-source, and performance covariates:
(1) Model 1 (Household level; DV = stated `Intent to contract` MSP among non-contracted functional waterpoints; N = 1,215 households clustered across 190 handpump groups; Pseudo R2 = 0.1641, Wald chi2 = 52.56, p < 0.05): `Management` w.r.t. `Community` -> `Individualist` OR = 0.762 (robust SE = 0.400, p = 0.605), `Bureaucratic` OR = 1.270 (robust SE = 0.672, p = 0.651); `Regular payments` OR = 2.662 (robust SE = 1.114, p = 0.019); `In favor of free water for vulnerable` OR = 0.537 (robust SE = 0.120, p = 0.005); `Concern that water supply is costly` OR = 0.532 (robust SE = 0.138, p = 0.015); `Handpump water for drinking` OR = 2.446 (robust SE = 1.062, p = 0.039); `Distance to next handpump` OR = 1.901 (robust SE = 0.617, p = 0.048); `Club` OR = 0.900 (SE = 0.373, p = 0.800); `Rules made by majority decision` OR = 0.609 (SE = 0.312, p = 0.333); `Women on committee` OR = 1.333 (SE = 0.509, p = 0.451); `Exclusion for not observing rules` OR = 0.388 (SE = 0.275, p = 0.181); `Penalties for non-payment` OR = 0.745 (SE = 0.183, p = 0.232).
(2) Model 2 (Handpump user-group level; DV = actual `Contract commitment` in Jan–Dec 2016; N = 254 functional handpumps; Pseudo R2 = 0.3025, Wald chi2 = 69.23, p < 0.001): `Management` w.r.t. `Community` -> `Individualist` OR = 1.549 (robust SE = 1.037, p = 0.513), `Bureaucratic` OR = 0.886 (robust SE = 0.720, p = 0.881); `Regular payments` OR = 3.149 (robust SE = 1.645, p = 0.028); `Distance to MSP office` OR = 0.852 (robust SE = 0.036, p = 0.000); `Electrical conductivity < 1500 uS` OR = 4.367 (robust SE = 2.799, p = 0.021); `Household grows crops` OR = 6.913 (robust SE = 6.863, p = 0.051); `pH > 7` OR = 2.941 (robust SE = 1.698, p = 0.062); `Women on committee` OR = 2.474 (robust SE = 1.217, p = 0.066); `Concern that water is unreliable` OR = 6.747 (robust SE = 7.392, p = 0.081); `Club` OR = 2.244 (robust SE = 1.049, p = 0.084); `Exclusion for not observing rules` OR = 1.519 (SE = 0.999, p = 0.524); `Penalties for non-payment` OR = 1.565 (SE = 0.692, p = 0.311).
(3) Descriptive uptake (Section 4.1, PDF p. 5; Fig. 3, p. 6): 22% of 300 active WDT handpumps signed contracts in year 1 (24% community, 16% individualist/private, 13% bureaucratic); Table 3 (PDF p. 9) reports unadjusted cross-culture mean differences in predictors.
raw_response.study_design_and_sample: Exploratory, non-causal observational cross-sectional analysis of multi-wave survey, water-quality, smart-sensor, and service-provider administrative data in rural Kwale County, Kenya (anchored on a 2013 census of 571 Afridev handpumps, excluding 112 waterpoints non-functional >1 year). Primary analytic samples: Model 1 analyzes N = 1,215 households clustered around 190 functional, non-contracting handpumps (Wave 3 survey, Sept–Nov 2016); Model 2 analyzes N = 254 functional sensor-fitted handpump user groups (Wave 2 household means, March–May 2015, linked to Jan–Dec 2016 contracting records).
